chunks: Zurarah and Muḥammad ibn Muslim said: We said to Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام,

A man did not find water, and the time for salat arrived, so he performed tayammum and prayed two rakʿahs. Then he found water. Should he invalidate the two rakʿahs, or cut them off, perform wudu, and then pray? He said: “No. Rather, he continues in his salat and completes it, and he does not invalidate it on account of the presence of water, because he entered it while in a state of taharah through tayammum.”
And Zurarah said: I said to him,

He entered it while in tayammum, then prayed one rakʿah, then invalidated his wudu, and then found water. He said: “He goes out, performs wudu, then builds upon what has passed of his salat which he prayed with tayammum.”

key_terms.أَحْدَثَ: incurred a nullifying event that broke ritual purity
key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ: the obligatory ritual prayer whose time has begun
key_terms.بِالتَّيَمُّمِ: by means of tayammum as the basis of ritual purity
key_terms.تَيَمَّمَ: performed tayammum as a substitute purification due to lack of water
key_terms.رَكْعَتَيْنِ: two units of prayer already performed
key_terms.طُهْرٍ: a valid state of ritual purity
key_terms.مُتَيَمِّمٌ: one who is in a state of purity by tayammum

ai.seo_question: If someone starts salat with tayammum and then finds water, should he stop and perform wudu?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on salat begun with tayammum when water is later found. If water is found without a new nullifying event, the prayer is completed as begun; but if one breaks purity and then finds water, he performs wudu and continues from what he had already prayed.
